    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Kimpton has a pretty cool “social password” concept, whereby you can receive extra perks for sharing a phrase at check-in. Kimpton generally has this promotion a couple of times per year — we last saw this in summer, and there’s now a upcoming password for winter.

    I’d like to talk about what the upcoming password is, share my experience using it, and also pose a question to Kimpton regulars about the least cringeworthy way to go about saying it.

    Kimpton is one of the cooler IHG hotel groups, and there are a variety of things that set Kimpton apart from other IHG brands. One of those things is the social password. The idea is that seasonally, Kimpton provides a phrase through social media that you’re supposed to say when you check-in, and if you do that, you’ll receive something extra.

    Recent findings suggest that the new Kimpton password is “this calls for something,” and it’s valid for stays between November 27, 2026, and February 28, 2027. So just say that when you check-in at a Kimpton property during the promotion period, and you’ll receive a surprise.

    Sources indicate that for those curious about what happens when you say the Kimpton password, I stayed at the Kimpton EPIC Miami some time back, which was my first Kimpton stay in quite a while (and I haven’t stayed at one since either). It was a good value as well, as I was able to use a free night award earned with the Fresh IHG One Rewards Premier Credit Card (learn more).

    I was curious what the benefit would be for using the password. So I shared the password with the front desk agent. At the conclusion of the check-in experience, he brought out a game show-style wheel. I might have spun too hard, as it must have gone around for about 30 seconds. Go figure I landed on the tile that just had me spin again.

    Then I spun again, and the prize was free parking. I had a car and was staying for two nights, and parking costs $44 per night. So using the Kimpton password saved me nearly $100 — score!!

    Sources indicate that based on looking at the wheel, it seems that some of the other prizes include a free welcome drink, free breakfast, free snacks, and a free movie. There were also a few empty squares, where I guess you don’t win anything. And I’m not sure what the alarm clock, car tipping over, or postcard of Miami get you. Regardless, I’d say those are some awesome prizes, and I got a great reward.

    Industry observers note that it’s cute how the Kimpton EPIC Miami makes a game of this. I know there’s a lot of inconsistency when it comes to this benefit across Kimpton properties. Some hotels provide meaningful perks (an upgrade, free, parking, etc.), like I got here, while other hotels provide a 19 cent branded koozie.

    It’s great that this has stuck around, given that it has presumably become increasingly popular. Years ago not everyone was on social media, so it was a good way to encourage people to follow Kimpton on X, Facebook, Instagram, etc. With the way the internet has evolved, times have changed a bit.

    It has been revealed that I’m sure I’m not the only one who finds the concept of saying a password at check-in to be kind of weird. So I think it’s fun to compare notes about how people share the password at the front desk. I find it awkward to just blurt out the password out of nowhere.

    So when I used this for my stay, I said “I guess I’m supposed to say [social password] as the social password?” That did the trick, but I’d be curious to hear how other Kimpton regulars go about this!

    In a recent development, between November 27, 2026, and February 28, 2027, Kimpton’s social password is “this calls for something.” Just state that phrase when you check-in at a Kimpton, and you should get some sort of a surprise. The gift will vary by property, so there’s no reason not to take advantage of this if staying at a Kimpton.

    The last time I used the password I got to spin a wheel at check-in, and then I ended up getting free parking, which was a value of $44 per night.

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that house Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., pictured at the U.S.
    • Republicans who want to accomplish as much as possible before Democrats take control of the House are confronting a new challenge: Attendance.
    • Thirty-two members – 21 Republicans, 10 Democrats, and one independent – did not vote in Thursday morning’s session before members headed out of town a day early for Thanksgiving break.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that house Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., pictured at the U.S. Capitol on Thursday, mentioned attendance is 'a great frustration.' (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Republicans who want to accomplish as much as possible before Democrats take control of the House are confronting a new challenge: Attendance.

    Thirty-two members – 21 Republicans, 10 Democrats, and one independent – did not vote in Thursday morning’s session before members headed out of town a day early for Thanksgiving break. This, a day after House GOP leadership pulled a procedural rule vote when it was clear the vote might fall short because of GOP no-demonstrates – and then canceled a planned Friday voting session.

    Recent findings suggest that the House has just 12 scheduled voting days left in the 119th Congress. And leaders who have at times struggled to ensure sufficient support for their agenda from the narrow majority now say they will work to make sure cases of senioritis don’t compound the problem, as both returning and nonreturning members have been part of the problem.

    "Attendance is a great frustration for me right now,” House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., told reporters Thursday. “We'll be addressing that with members.".

    “We want to run through the tape and finish strong, but we can't do that unless people are present at work, so that's our challenge,” Johnson continued.

    Sources indicate that of 13 roll call votes in the House since the midterms, all but one has had a double-digit number of no-reveals; for five of the 13, more than 30 members did not vote. The average number of members not voting has more than doubled since the midterm elections, compared to the final 13 roll call votes beforehand.

    Johnson has just a few more weeks before he steps out of the spotlight and Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, takes over the GOP conference as minority leader. But his members are still counting on him to get them back to Washington.

    “I think there's going to be some serious conversations over the phone, behind the scenes over the weekend,” Rep. Michael Cloud, R-Texas, said. “We all took an oath of office. We have a sworn duty to be here. We're still being paid to be here, and you have to show up and do the job.”.

    And it's not just leadership that's frustrated with their missing colleagues this week.

    Industry observers note that “There is, no question,” Rep. Pat Harrigan, R-N.C., who narrowly won reelection, responded when asked whether there was frustration in the caucus over members' absences.

    According to recent reports, “I don't know what you do with people that don't understand the concept of duty,” Harrigan said. “I mean, look, you signed up for a two-year term. You execute your two-year term, no matter what happens along the way politically. You have an obligation both to your constituency and to your country to be here, so the fact that they're not self-motivated to be here, I don't think that there's really much that you can do.”.

    It has been revealed that attendance has also been a bipartisan problem. A group of House Democrats, including members of leadership, faced harsh criticism from party activists for not returning to the chamber in time for a vote related to a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

    While Republican leadership grapples with the fallout from the party’s election losses earlier this month, lawmakers still face a slew of legislative items as Congress looks ahead to the holidays and a government shutdown looms.

    Many Republicans want to see a party-line defense spending bill cross the finish line, while the NDAA remains in treacherous territory and Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act has been dark for months.

    However, the frustration does not lie solely with absent House members.

    It has been revealed that “The Senate needs to do their job,” Rep. John McGuire, R-Va., said. “I know we had a hard time in the midterms. History doesn't favor the party in the president's office, but we passed the Save America Act five times here. It goes over there, nothing. We've got a farm bill, nothing. We got an NDAA. We got so many things.”.

    • American Airlines is at the moment offering a rare elevated promotion on purchasing AAdvantage miles.
    • While that’s not a price at which I’d proactively pick up miles, there are definitely some situations where that could represent a good value, if you have an immediate use in mind, especially for first and business class travel.
    • Note that offers like this are extremely rare — while American offers a 40% off promotion on buying miles consistently, the 50% off promotion seems to come around just once or twice per year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    American Airlines is at the moment offering a rare elevated promotion on purchasing AAdvantage miles. Through December 2, 2026, AAdvantage members can purchase miles with up to a 50% discount, which is potentially an opportunity to buy miles for 1.88 cents each.

    While that’s not a price at which I’d proactively pick up miles, there are definitely some situations where that could represent a good value, if you have an immediate use in mind, especially for first and business class travel.

    Note that offers like this are extremely rare — while American offers a 40% off promotion on buying miles consistently, the 50% off promotion seems to come around just once or twice per year.

    Link: Buy American Airlines AAdvantage miles with a discount.

    Between 12:01AM CT on November 27 and 11:59PM CT on December 2, 2026, American AAdvantage is offering up to a 50% discount (or 100% bonus, if you prefer) on buying miles. The offer is tiered, and you get a bigger discount the more miles you buy, as follows:.

    As you can see, you need to buy a lot of miles to get the best price!

    Ordinarily American sells AAdvantage miles for 3.5 cents each pre-tax, or 3.76 cents after factoring in the 7.5% federal excise tax. That’s before any discounts or bonuses. In this case if you max out the promotion and buy 500,000 AAdvantage miles, you’d pay a total of $9,406.25, which comes out to 1.88 cents per mile (that factors in the 7.5% tax).

    Keep in mind that American Airlines mileage purchases are non-refundable, and buying AAdvantage miles doesn’t count toward your Loyalty Points total (other than any amount you may spend on an eligible credit card). Purchased miles typically post nearly instantly, but in some cases, it can take up to four hours for them to post.

    The 50% discount is the best price we’ve seen from American AAdvantage in recent years, and again, it only comes around once or twice per year. With the standard 40% off promotion on buying miles, you’d ordinarily pay 2.26 cents per mile.

    Sources indicate that the American AAdvantage program ordinarily allows members to buy at most 300,000 miles per account per calendar year, before factoring in any bonuses. However, during this promotion, that cap has been increased to 500,000 miles. AAdvantage accounts less than 30 days old aren’t eligible to buy American Airlines miles. Miles can only be purchased in 1,000-point increments.

    The process of buying American Airlines miles is easy — the easiest way is to simply follow this link. Alternatively, you can go to aa.com, click on “AAdvantage” at the top of the page, and then click on “Buy, gift or transfer miles.”.

    Yes, you absolutely can buy American Airlines miles, you just have to be aware of a few restrictions. For one, your account needs to be at least 30 days old. On top of that, you have to stay within the annual cap.

    It’s possible to buy miles for yourself or others, but you’ll need to be sure you use the right account to make the purchase.

    Is this a good deal? At 1.88 cents per mile, the current promotion is 50% below the standard price. That matches the best deal we’ve tracked. It’s 0.38 cents above our 1.5-cent valuation of AAdvantage miles.

    Sources indicate that unlike Delta SkyMiles and United MileagePlus, American AAdvantage continues to publish award charts for travel on partner airlines, and redemption rates are largely quite good, especially for travel in premium cabins on partner airlines. Among the “significant three” carriers in the US, I tend to think AAdvantage has the best redemption opportunities.

    I find the cost of business class redemptions to be excellent in many cases. There are instances where it could make sense to pick up miles during a promotion with a short term use in mind. Just to give a few examples of some of my favorite uses of AAdvantage miles (all redemption rates are one-way):.

    Now, unfortunately the catch is that partner award availability is in many instances quite limited. For airlines like Cathay Pacific, Etihad, and Qatar Airways, the airlines now largely restrict premium awards to members of their own frequent flyer programs. So definitely do your research before buying any miles.

    Recent findings suggest that another thing worth mentioning is that if you redeem for travel on British Airways, get ready to pay huge carrier imposed surcharges, which could be hundreds of dollars on a long haul premium cabin trip. So that wouldn’t be my preferred use of American Airlines miles.

    American Airlines belongs to the oneworld alliance, so you can redeem AAdvantage miles on all oneworld airlines.

    On top of that, you can redeem miles on some of American’s other partner airlines, including Aer Lingus, Air Tahiti Nui, China Southern, Etihad Airways, and GOL Airlines, among others.

    Everyone will value mileage currencies differently, and based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider AAdvantage miles to be worth 1.5 cents each. However, I tend to value points pretty conservatively, and there are many ways to get way more value from AAdvantage miles than that.

    According to recent reports, american AAdvantage miles don’t expire as long as you have at least some account activity once every 24 months. Eligible activity includes earning or redeeming AAdvantage miles in any quantity.

    There are lots of great ways to earn American miles aside from outright buying them:.

    Through December 2, 2026, American AAdvantage is offering a discount on buying miles. The program is offering up to a 50% discount when you buy American Airlines miles, which is an opportunity to buy them for 1.88 cents each. While I wouldn’t speculatively buy miles at this cost, with a specific use in mind, there could be value with this offer.

    #158367. Industry News: Citi AAdvantage Executive Card Review: Is The Admirals Club Perk Worth It?

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 18m • 📚 Deep Dive (3632 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Citi AAdvantage Executive Card Review: Is The Admirals Club Perk Worth It?

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3632 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (formerly known as the Citi AAdvantage Executive World Elite Mastercard) is American Airlines’ most premium co-branded credit card, as part of the Citi partnership.
    • Industry observers note that if you ask me, it’s one of the best value premium airline credit cards out there, and it’s also the airline credit card with the strongest lounge access perks.
    • In this post, I’d like to take an in-depth look at the Citi AA Executive Card, with my Citi AAdvantage Executive Card review.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (formerly known as the Citi AAdvantage Executive World Elite Mastercard) is American Airlines’ most premium co-branded credit card, as part of the Citi partnership. While the Citi AA Executive Card has a steep annual fee, it offers strong perks, ranging from an Admirals Club membership, to the ability to supercharge your AAdvantage elite status, to credits that can help offset the annual fee.

    Industry observers note that if you ask me, it’s one of the best value premium airline credit cards out there, and it’s also the airline credit card with the strongest lounge access perks. While products like the American Express Platinum Card® (learn more) and Chase Sapphire Reserve® Card (learn more) might typically be the first that come to mind when people consider premium cards, this one could make a lot more sense if you’re a frequent American flyer.

    In this post, I’d like to take an in-depth look at the Citi AA Executive Card, with my Citi AAdvantage Executive Card review. I think this is especially important in light of the card’s recent refresh, where we saw the annual fee increase, but also saw upcoming perks added.

    Link: Learn more about the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard®.

    Let me start by briefly summarizing the key details of the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card:.

    This is the ideal card if you value American Admirals Club lounge access, if you’re going for elite status with American AAdvantage, or if you can just make the credits on the card work. If you’re just an occasional American flyer, there are probably more affordable options that will be easier to justify in the long term. However, with the card’s significant welcome bonus, there’s a huge incentive to give this card a try.

    One of the reasons that you’ll want to consider applying for the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is because of the excellent welcome bonus it has. Of course that has to be balanced with the annual fee, and you also have to take into account the eligibility requirements, so let’s go through those details for the Citi AA Executive Card.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card currently has a welcome bonus of 80,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $8,000 within the first three months.

    Personally, I value American AAdvantage miles at ~1.5 cents each, so to me, those miles are worth about $1,200. That’s an excellent bonus, especially for a card that also offers a lot of value in the long run. There are so many great uses of AAdvantage miles, including for travel on partner airlines.

    For what it’s worth, I value Delta SkyMiles at 1.1 cents each, and United MileagePlus miles at 1.3 cents each, so these are the most valuable miles among the “massive three” carriers, based on my math.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card bonus miles aren’t available to those who have received a new cardmember bonus for this card in the past 48 months (however, you are eligible if you’ve had a different American Airlines credit card, including if you’ve received a bonus on a different product).

    Then there are the typical rules for Citi credit card applications, including that you can apply for at most one card with Citi every eight days, and at most two cards every 65 days.

    In a recent development, there’s not a consistent credit score that you need to get approved for the card, though I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected, as it’s one of only many factors that determines eligibility.

    Recent findings suggest that the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card has a $695 annual fee. There’s also a lot of value to adding authorized owners (as I’ll discuss below). You can expect to pay a total of $175 for up to three authorized users (so potentially under $60 each), and then each authorized user after that costs $175.

    Keep in mind that if you’re a Citigold customer, you can receive a $145 annual rebate on your annual fee, which is a nice perk.

    When it comes to spending money on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, here’s the rewards structure:.

    In terms of the reward for spending, there are potentially better cards for purchasing airline tickets, and also better cards for everyday spending. However, keep in mind that the most compelling reason to spend money on the card is in order to earn elite status with American Airlines. American Airlines uses its Loyalty Points system for status qualification, and credit card spending can help you earn status.

    American’s elite requirements are right now as follows, and you earn one Loyalty Point for every dollar spent on an American Airlines credit card:.

    Industry observers note that spending on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card could earn you elite status, which I know will interest many. That’s the primary reason you’ll want to consider this card for spending.

    I do want to specifically point out one thing that throws people off — you earn one Loyalty Point per dollar spent on the card, unrelated to how many miles you earn for spending. In other words, if you’re making an American Airlines purchase, you’d earn 4x AAdvantage redeemable miles, but only 1x Loyalty Points on the purchase as such.

    In addition to earning one Loyalty Point for every dollar spent on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you can also earn up to 40,000 Loyalty Points every year just for being a cardmember:.

    Industry observers note that in other words, if you have this card, you’d only otherwise need to earn 170,000 Loyalty Points for Executive Platinum status, since this card would get you a boost of 30,000 Loyalty Points at that level. Those Loyalty Points can be earned in a variety of ways, ranging from flying, to online shopping, to credit card spending, to booking vacation packages. Either way, this Loyalty Points boost would be quite the advantage in terms of qualifying for Loyalty Point Rewards, and even upgrade priority.

    Sources indicate that the AAdvantage elite qualifying year goes from the beginning of March until the end of February of the following year. You don’t need to have the card at the beginning of the year to take advantage of this, so even if you open the card during the membership year, you could still earn 40,000 bonus Loyalty Points for that year (in other words, the credits can be retroactive).

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card has no foreign transaction fees, so this can be a good option for purchases abroad.

    While you’ll want to consult the full cardmember agreement and guide to benefits, the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers useful travel protection, including trip cancellation coverage, trip interruption coverage, trip delay protection, lost baggage protection, rental car coverage, and more.

    So this is a good card to potentially use for travel purchases, since you have to put them on your card to take advantage of those benefits.

    One of the main reasons you may want to get the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is because of the lounge access perks that the card offers. Having the Citi AA Executive Card is the best way to access Admirals Clubs. Let’s discuss how that works.

    In a recent development, the primary cardmember on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card receives a full Admirals Club membership, including guesting privileges. That in and of itself is a reason this card makes sense.

    While Admirals Clubs aren’t anything to get too excited about, they are improving nicely, in terms of design, and also in terms of the quality of food and beverages. I also appreciate the expansion of the Provisions by Admirals Club concept, whereby the airline offers Admirals Club members grab & go facility, where they can get some drinks or snacks to go before their flight.

    Ordinarily, if you were to buy a comparable Admirals Club membership with guesting privileges, you’d pay a minimum of $1,200 per year.

    By getting an Admirals Club membership with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you’re saving $505-705 right off the bat.

    Note that while you can redeem miles for an Admirals Club membership, it’s a terrible value, as you’re getting only a cent per mile.

    What you get with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is a full Admirals Club membership, so you don’t even have to bring your credit card, as your membership will be linked to your AAdvantage number:.

    Admirals Club members don’t get access to Flagship Lounges, as that access is determined based on the ticket you purchased rather than any membership.

    Industry observers note that many people may be considering applying for the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card shortly before taking an American Airlines trip. How soon after being approved for the card does your Admirals Club membership kick in?

    Sources indicate that since the primary cardmember gets a full Admirals Club membership, it’s linked to their AAdvantage account. Many may be surprised to learn that this membership could very well kick in before you even receive your credit card in the mail, and you don’t even need your card to enter a lounge.

    Fortunately, there’s an easy way to tell if your Admirals Club membership has been activated. To figure it out, pretend that you’re signing up for an Admirals Club membership. Go to this page, enter your AAdvantage number, last name, and password.

    If your account has already been updated to reflect the Admirals Club membership, you’ll see that the next page indicates “1-Year Citi AADV Exec CC Membership.”.

    If it hasn’t been updated, you’ll see that it gives you the option of choosing what kind of membership you want to purchase.

    Note that this only works for the primary cardmember. Since the authorized owners don’t get a full Admirals Club membership, they wouldn’t show up as being eligible online. Authorized users need to present the physical Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, since there’s no membership linked to their AAdvantage account.

    Industry observers note that the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card also offers Admirals Club access for authorized owners. As I explained above, you can add up to three authorized users for a total of $175, which potentially comes out to under $60 per authorized user. I’d say that’s a real sweet spot, since securing lounge access for friends and family for under $60 each is an amazing value.

    Note that authorized consumers receive Admirals Club access and not a membership, so there are the restrictions:.

    For the purposes of accessing Admirals Clubs this is more or less the same as an outright membership.

    On the next page, you’ll be able to manage authorized consumers, including adding and removing them.

    You’ll just need their name to add them, and you have the choice of whether or not you want to give them permission to access your online account.

    Make sure you trust all your authorized owners, since any charges they incur will be your responsibility.

    The primary reason to get the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is because of the great welcome bonus, ability to earn status with spending, ability to receive 40,000 Loyalty Points annually just for being a cardmember, and Admirals Club benefit.

    However, the Citi AA Executive Card offers some other perks that could add a lot of value for card members. These perks range from priority check-in at business class counters, to early boarding, to inflight or Admirals Club credits, to savings with American Airlines Vacations, Lyft, Avis, Budget, Global Entry, or TSA PreCheck, to elite status with Avis and Omni.

    Below is what you need to know about all the other perks of the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card.

    Sources indicate that those with the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card receive a first checked bag free on domestic American Airlines itineraries not just for themselves, but also for up to eight companions traveling on the same reservation. There’s no need to actually pay for the ticket with your Citi AAdvantage Executive Card — you just have to make sure it’s linked to your AAdvantage account (this benefit applies for the primary cardmember only).

    American ordinarily charges $45-50 for the first checked bag, so that’s a $90-100 value per person roundtrip (and if you had eight companions all checking a bag, that would be a value of $810-900).

    Recent findings suggest that one thing that sometimes throws off cardmembers is that this benefit doesn’t work for international flights, and it doesn’t work for a second bag, if your fare includes one bag. So just understand this is exclusively a first checked bag benefit on domestic flights.

    In a recent development, for being the primary cardmember on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card you receive several valuable airport benefits, including priority check-in, priority airport screening, and early boarding. These are all features that can save you time and money.

    There’s no need to show your card, as these perks should automatically be reflected with your ticket when you have your credit card linked to your AAdvantage account (which is automatic when you’re the primary cardmember).

    According to recent reports, the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers up to $500 in statement credits per calendar year toward American Airlines Vacations purchases. American Airlines Vacations is the carrier’s vacation package portal. This credit is semi-annual, meaning you can take advantage of a $250 credit every six months (once in January through June, and once in July through December).

    Industry observers note that this applies for a booking of two or more travel components, like a flight, car reservation, or hotel booking. Many people find American Airlines Vacations to be a great deal, and a good way to earn bonus Loyalty Points.

    It has been revealed that the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers up to $200 in InKind credits every year. This comes in the form of a $100 semi-annual credit, with one being available January 1 through June 30, and the other being available July 1 through December 31. This can be used across multiple meals, and tips aren’t covered by the credit. Either the primary cardmember or authorized customers can use the perk, though authorized users don’t get extra credits.

    InKind is my favorite dining rewards app, and to me, this is basically good as cash. I dine at InKind restaurants constantly, as there are some really high quality restaurants on the list, so I value this fresh card perk immensely. If you’re new to InKind, make sure you also register through a refer-a-friend link, so you can get an extra credit.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers up to $180 in Lyft credits every year. This comes in the form of a $15 Lyft credit each month after taking three eligible rides. The Lyft credit expires 30 days after it’s issued. Either the primary cardmember or authorized customers can use the perk, though authorized users don’t get extra credits. Admittedly this requires quite a bit of effort to use, so not everyone will get value from that.

    Recent findings suggest that just for having the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you can receive up to $120 back on eligible Avis or Budget rentals every calendar year. Just charge an eligible pre-paid rental to your card each year, and you’ll receive a statement credit up to the $120 limit. This can be used toward a single rental or multiple rentals made directly with Avis or Budget. If you rent with Avis and Budget with any frequency, this could be worth face value.

    Just for having the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you can receive up to $100 in statement credits every calendar year toward spending onboard American flights, or in Admirals Clubs. So you can use this credit to purchase everything from premium drinks or snacks on flights, to premium alcoholic drinks in Admirals Clubs.

    Just charge the eligible purchase to your card, and you’ll be reimbursed automatically, with no registration required.

    Recent findings suggest that the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit once every four years, which is worth up to $120. Simply charge the purchase to your card and it will automatically be reimbursed. You don’t have to be the one signing up — you can always pay for a friend or family member who is signing up instead.

    Personally, I always recommend applying for Global Entry, because Global Entry automatically comes with TSA PreCheck, while the inverse isn’t true.

    According to recent reports, the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card now offers some perks with Omni Hotels & Resorts. For those not familiar, Omni operates around 50 properties in the United States and Canada, so there’s value in getting extra perks at these hotels. Specifically:.

    In a recent development, to take advantage of this, you’ll want to enroll before your stay, book your stay direct with Omni, and pay with the card. If you stay at Omni properties with any frequencies, this is quite a nice value-add, if you ask me.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card offers complimentary Avis President’s Club status, with enrollment available through August 31, 2028.

    Avis President’s Club status offers a variety of perks, including car upgrades, expedited service, complimentary additional drivers, and more. If you rent from Avis, you should definitely be able to get some value from this.

    Industry observers note that the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is a World Legend Mastercard, meaning that it comes with quite a few benefits you may not be familiar with. In addition to the concierge service, there are also savings and other perks with a variety of businesses, ranging from DoorDash to HelloFresh.

    Let me once again state that this card used to be known as the Citi AAdvantage Executive World Elite Mastercard, before recently being rebranded as a World Legend Mastercard.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is a lucrative card that I personally have and also recommend, but only if you’re a frequent flyer with American. If you fly American with any frequency then an Admirals Club membership is valuable, and this is the best way to get an Admirals Club membership. There can even be value in adding up to three authorized owners, which will cost a total of $175, as they’d get Admirals Club access as well.

    It has been revealed that in addition to lounge access, the Citi AA Executive Card offers up to 40,000 Loyalty Points per year (even without spending money on the card), which can make a substantial difference for anyone chasing status with American. Furthermore, the card potentially offers hundreds of dollars in credits per year, which can help offset the annual fee.

    In a recent development, however, this isn’t a card that I’d use for my everyday spending unless I specifically valued the added Loyalty Points from spending. Otherwise, there are much more rewarding cards for everyday spending, and I’d just hold onto this card for the very strong perks, including lounge access, and the bonus Loyalty Points without a spending requirement.

    For my mental accounting purposes, I take the $695 annual fee, and then subtract the $200 InKind credit, which I consider to basically be worth face value. That really takes the “out of pocket” on the card to $495 per year for me, which is an amazing deal for the Admirals Club membership and bonus Loyalty Points.

    While the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is American’s most premium credit card, it’s also worth being aware of the Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® (learn more), which has a $350 annual fee. There are lots of reasons to consider that card, including an excellent welcome bonus. Among other things:.

    I think there’s potentially merit to having both cards, especially if you value earning the Loyalty Points bonuses. Otherwise I’d say the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card is easier to justify if you’re an occasional American flyer, while I think the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is easier to justify if you value an Admirals Club membership.

    The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card isn’t for everyone. If you’re not a frequent flyer on American then you shouldn’t consider this card. However, if you are a frequent flyer on American then this card is totally for you.

    While Admirals Clubs aren’t anything to get too excited about, there’s still huge value in the complimentary snacks and drinks, free Wi-Fi and quiet places to sit, and access to an agent in the event your flight has irregular operations.

    Even beyond the Admirals Club membership, the card offers other useful perks, like the ability to earn Loyalty Points, priority services with American, and the ability to receive credits with American Airlines Vacations, InKind, Avis, Budget, Lyft, and more.

    Sources indicate that I’ve had the Citi AA Executive Card for years, and love it. If you don’t yet have the card, this is a good time to apply, given the offer that’s available.

    If you want to learn more about the Citi Executive AAdvantage Card or want to apply, follow this link.

    It has been revealed that membership is free and takes no more information than commenting as a guest. Earn status points for good contributions, and see fewer ads as your status grows.

    Industry News: Appeals court stands by LaMonica McIver ruling

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., is seen on Capitol Hill last December.
    • LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., faced a setback Thursday in her effort to ditch charges tied to a scuffle during an oversight visit at an immigration detention facility last year, as a federal appeals court declined to reconsider its decision to let the case move forward.
    • Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit leaves in place a 2-1 opinion from August which held that McIver was not immune from the charges, which stemmed from a confrontation between visiting members of Congress and federal agents while at the Delaney Hall facility in Newark.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., is seen on Capitol Hill last December. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Recent findings suggest that rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., faced a setback Thursday in her effort to ditch charges tied to a scuffle during an oversight visit at an immigration detention facility last year, as a federal appeals court declined to reconsider its decision to let the case move forward.

    The decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit leaves in place a 2-1 opinion from August which held that McIver was not immune from the charges, which stemmed from a confrontation between visiting members of Congress and federal agents while at the Delaney Hall facility in Newark. McIver has challenged the charges, arguing that her visit fell under the “speech or debate” immunity she has as a member of Congress because she was there to inspect detention conditions.

    It has been revealed that in a statement McIver said she and her attorneys were looking at “every possible option” in response to the appeals court ruling. Her statement invoked the Trump administration’s threats to treat oversight efforts as criminal conduct and said “we are all one step closer to a world in which the president of the United States can try to imprison people simply because he does not like what they stand for.”.

    “Donald Trump continues to send warning shots to Democrats in Congress and in all levels of power — but their case against me right now, in broad daylight, goes well beyond a warning. Because of a weaponized Department of Justice and because I dared to do my job and conduct oversight of ICE, I am facing 17 years in prison,” McIver said in her statement.

    Following Thursday’s decision on rehearing, McIver could next ask the Supreme Court to weigh in on the case.

    The August majority opinion from Judge Cindy Chung, which Thursday’s decision leaves in place, noted that two of the three charges against McIver did not fall under the immunity, which is limited to legislative acts. The majority sent the third charge back to the lower court for another ruling.

    “We have considered the ‘nature’ of the charged conduct and concluded it is unambiguously non-legislative,” the judge wrote.

    Separately, Judge Thomas Ambro partially dissented to offer a different approach to the case. Ambro would have required the trial judge to more closely examine the exact conduct McIver was charged with, as well as to examine whether the Trump administration targeted her because of her political views.

    “I would allow her discovery into the truth of the matter — not only for her own sake but to safeguard the independence of our legislative bodies,” Ambro wrote.

    According to recent reports, ambro did not vote on whether the full 3rd Circuit should rehear the case. Three judges voted to have the full 3rd Circuit hear McIver’s case, and Judge Emil Bove, a former Trump administration official and former personal attorney for the president, did not participate in the vote.

    It has been revealed that the criminal case started shortly after the Delaney Hall visit in May 2025, as prosecutors alleged that McIver assaulted federal agents during a scuffle around Newark Mayor Ras Baraka. Officials arrested Baraka that day and charged him with trespassing, but later dropped those charges.

    Court filings in the case alleged that McIver struck agents during the confrontation. McIver has argued that she was effectively being charged for doing her job and federal agents were interfering with her attempts to inspect the facility.

    Recent findings suggest that earlier this year, Judge Jamel K. Semper of the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey disagreed and ruled that the case could move forward.

    #158363. Ryanair Now Withholds Free Seats Until Just Before Departure, Blames Customer Feedback

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (854 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Ryanair Now Withholds Free Seats Until Just Before Departure, Blames Customer Feedback

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ryanair has quietly updated its policy for how it assigns seats to those people who don’t pay the seat assignment fee, as reported by The Irish Times.
    • According to recent reports, ryanair is known for being an unapologetic ultra low cost carrier.
    • However, the way the airline is randomly allocating seats has quietly changed as of late October 2026, coinciding with the start of the winter schedule.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ryanair has quietly updated its policy for how it assigns seats to those people who don’t pay the seat assignment fee, as reported by The Irish Times. While I wouldn’t consider this to be anything unreasonable, what I’m amused by is the carrier’s justification. The airline claims that it’s doing this due to customer feedback, rather than to generate more revenue.

    According to recent reports, ryanair is known for being an unapologetic ultra low cost carrier. The airline has low base fares, and then charges fees for just about everything. Among other things, the airline charges to assign seats in advance, and those who don’t pay for specific seat assignments are just randomly assigned seats (and often in a rather punitive way).

    However, the way the airline is randomly allocating seats has quietly changed as of late October 2026, coinciding with the start of the winter schedule. Historically, the airline has automatically assigned seats to passengers without seat assignments around 24 hours before departure.

    In a recent development, some passengers seemed to “game” this, and would essentially “gamble.” What they’d do is wait until 24 hours out to see what seat they were assigned for free. Then if they weren’t happy with their automatic seat assignment, they could still pay to assign a better seat.

    Under the new policy, the airline still problems a boarding pass up to 24 hours out, but without a seat assignment. Then the boarding pass automatically shows the seat assignment within four hours of departure.

    Sources indicate that the logic here seems pretty clear — some people do care somewhat about where they sit, but want to avoid fees if they can. By withholding seat assignments until hours before departure, passengers are presumably more likely to pay for seat assignments in advance, to avoid that uncertainty.

    Ryanair has confirmed this seat assignment policy change in a statement, sharing that “the timing of the allocation of free random seats is determined at all times by the airline.” Right, nobody disputes that the airline has the right to do this.

    So, what’s the logic for this policy change? According to the airline, it’s “to allow those passengers who wish to select their preferred seat more time to do so. We had a number of complaints this summer that passengers could not book their preferred seat on the day of travel as it had been already randomly allocated as a free seat up to 24 hours prior to departure.”.

    The Ryanair representative went on to say that “passengers who choose a free of charge random seat clearly don’t mind where they sit, and their digital boarding pass is automatically updated between three to four hours prior to departure, which is well before they arrive at either their departure airport or their boarding gate.”.

    Ryanair is of course within its rights to have this policy, but I think the logic is pretty obvious, and it’s to generate more revenue. After all, 24 hours out people would see what they were randomly assigned at online check-in, and would still have a lot of choices if they wanted to pay for seats, since most people don’t check-in online exactly at the 24-hour mark.

    In a recent development, but within a few hours of departure, virtually everyone has checked in online, and not many seats will be left. So I imagine the goal is to condition more customers to pay for seat assignments in advance. I love the claim that customers complained that their preferred seats on the day of travel were randomly allocated to others for free:.

    Recent findings suggest that ryanair has a latest policy for automatic seat allocations. In the past, the airline would automatically assign seats to passengers 24 hours out, giving them quite the window to “gamble” on the free seat assignment, and then pay for a different seat assignment if they weren’t happy with the free one.

    Recent findings suggest that the airline has now started only assigning free seats at most four hours out. The airline claims that this is due to customer feedback, so that passengers have more time to assign their choice of paid seats. However, I imagine that’s not quite accurate, and this is instead about conditioning people to pay for seat assignments, rather than “gambling” on the free allocations.

    What do you make of this Ryanair seating policy change?

    #158362. Maine senators at odds over credit for earmarks

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (930 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Maine senators at odds over credit for earmarks

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Collins took sole responsibility for a larger share of Maine earmarks.
    • After a bruising reelection defeat, Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, is ready to play hardball.
    • Eager to show how much she's delivered for her constituents, Collins took the lion's share of credit in her committee's fiscal 2027 spending bills for Maine earmarks — at the expense of her delegation colleague, independent Angus King, who caucuses with Democrats.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Collins took sole responsibility for a larger share of Maine earmarks. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    After a bruising reelection defeat, Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, is ready to play hardball.

    Eager to show how much she's delivered for her constituents, Collins took the lion's share of credit in her committee's fiscal 2027 spending bills for Maine earmarks — at the expense of her delegation colleague, independent Angus King, who caucuses with Democrats.

    The amount of earmarks King secured fell dramatically compared to his previous year's total in Senate Appropriations Committee bills, as Collins took sole credit for most earmarks both senators had requested.

    The power play has instigated a dispute over how to award credit for "congressionally directed spending," better known as earmarks. It has also raised questions about a Senate rule that requires committee leaders to disclose the name of each senator who requested projects to be included in a spending bill before it can move on the floor.

    It’s undeniable that as the chair of the spending panel, Collins has more influence over which projects reach the final bills than her delegation mate. Collins spokesperson Phoebe Keller said that since available earmark funding is split into separate pots for the majority and minority to dole out, the bills reflect which of those funding sources was tapped to provide money to the relevant projects.

    Keller said that Collins deserves sole credit for the contested projects, as listed in the reports accompanying the bills.

    "When only Collins is listed, it reflects only she chose to fund the project,” Keller remarked.

    A Democratic committee aide contested that characterization, saying that traditionally all requesters are named regardless of which party’s funding allocation is tapped for a project.

    “The handling of these particular projects is a clear departure from the norm and will need to be rectified in conference negotiations,” the aide said.

    King is credited with approximately $54 million in fiscal 2027 earmarks in the bills Collins released this month, including joint projects with Collins. That's down from around $231 million in the Senate's fiscal 2026 bills, according to a CQ Roll Call analysis.

    Sources indicate that last year, King and Collins were both listed on 75 of the 77 projects that both requested that were included in the Senate bills, with just two carrying only Collins’ name. This year, Collins claimed sole responsibility for over $125 million in projects that both she and King requested, approximately two-thirds of the joint requests.

    While King’s overall requests fell by more than $200 million this year versus last, his success in securing requested funds plummeted at a far greater rate with less credit for overlapping projects.

    The joint requests for which Collins claimed sole credit include five for the Maine Department of Transportation in the Transportation-HUD bill, including $10.7 million for northern freight rail improvements; $9.6 million for Route 26 reconstruction in Oxford; and $7.2 million for improvements in Rockport, among others.

    In the Labor-HHS-Education bill, projects Collins took sole credit for include $4 million for the University of Maine for biology laboratory equipment and just over $4 million for the creation of a modern emergency helipad at Lincoln Hospital.

    And the Interior-Environment bill features $4 million each for wastewater improvements in Limestone and Kennebec that both Collins and King asked for but are only attributed to Collins, among others.

    Similarly, the Agriculture, Commerce-Justice-Science and Homeland Security bills all include a project requested by both senators that only Collins is listed as securing in the bill.

    The outgoing Appropriations chair’s ability to fuel billions of dollars in federal funding for her state during her career was the centerpiece of her ultimately unsuccessful campaign for reelection, which she lost to Democrat Troy Jackson.

    As written, the draft bills appear to risk running afoul of a Senate rule that requires the committee’s chair to identify each senator who requested projects in a bill online at least 48 hours before a vote to advance the legislation on the floor.

    The relevant rule, Senate Rule 44, states that it is out of order to vote on a motion to proceed to consider a bill unless the chairman of the committee certifies that “each congressionally directed spending item . . . has been identified through lists, charts, or other similar means including the name of each Senator who submitted a request to the committee for each item so identified.”.

    That information must be “available on a publicly accessible congressional website in a searchable format at least 48 hours before such vote.”.

    A King spokesman called on the spending panel to add his name to the relevant requests.

    “We believe this must have been an oversight and assume the committee will update the requests —per Senate rules — once it’s called to their attention,” King spokesman Matthew Felling said.

    The bills released by Collins are drafts, and no floor action on final fiscal 2027 spending bills is expected this Congress. There’s limited time left before the Dec. 11 spending deadline, when all current funding is set to expire, and Democrats want to wait to negotiate final bills until they retake majorities in both chambers next year.

    But to comply with the rule, before the bills reach the floor the reports accompanying the bills, that includes the earmark tables, may have to be rewritten to list King on the contested projects, or the committee may need to disclose the information elsewhere online.

    Both chambers unveiled stricter ethics guidelines surrounding earmarks in 2021 when the practice returned after a decade-long ban.

    Peter Cohn contributed to this report.

Mike Wagenheim’s November 24 upgrade on the reported TSA intervention Wagenheim’s earlier report cited two sources saying United knew of up to six additional crew members who’d expressed support for terrorist groups. United’s pilots union spokesman declined to discuss individual cases. He said the Air Line Pilots Association has a professional standards committee and legal team that assess accusations against its ethics code and United’s workplace guidelines. Israeli officials confirmed the restriction after receiving allegations that he’d expressed support for Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and Hezbollah. But United said he wasn’t right now flying, having been on leave since 2024. He flew Boeing 737s and wasn’t qualified on long haul aircraft. Apparently there was material showing Iranian leadership imagery and mourning civilians killed in strikes. There are claims of Hezbollah support and that there was a video of him kissing the regime’s emblem. United Pilot Celebrated October 7 Rapes And Murders As ‘Bravery’ I first wrote about Ibrahim Mossallam in November 2023, after his Facebook description of the October 7 attack as “resistance by a brave people.” United removed him from service with pay but he was reported back flying. On October 6, 2026, after the flydubai pilot sought to use his plane as a missile to attack Israel, United told me: We have withheld this pilot from service pending an ongoing review. There were also reports that he returned after just a day, and that two colleagues had given up first class seats to monitor him in the cockpit. United subsequently denied both accounts. A reported claimed the union blocked his firing. TSA Can Order A Pilot Out Of The Cockpit It was striking that the reported order came from TSA. It has authority that extends well beyond passenger checkpoints. Under federal law, a TSA determination that a pilot poses, or is suspected of posing, a terrorism or passenger safety threat requires the Federal Aviation Administration to take action against the pilot’s certificate. It says the pilot’s “TSA credential” was revoked and describes that as Known Crewmember access. The September 30 flydubai cockpit attack makes the concern concrete. He had satisfied the licensing, good conduct and security requirements for the job, and those checks had failed to uncover his extremist intentions. Under federal law, a TSA determination that a pilot poses, or is suspected of posing, a terrorism or passenger safety threat requires the Federal Aviation Administration to take action against the pilot’s certificate. TSA can request that the action take effect immediately. It can also glitch mandatory security directives to airlines. However, it isn’t clear from the report what legal mechanism is claimed to have been used and doesn’t report an FAA certificate action.     #158358. Industry News: Warning For Families Traveling To California: Latest Booster Seat Law Covers Kids Through Age 15

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 19m • 📚 Deep Dive (3768 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Warning For Families Traveling To California: Latest Booster Seat Law Covers Kids Through Age 15

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3768 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that I have a California trip coming up with my family.
    • She could fit the belt in our car at home and need a booster in the SUV we get assigned to, but she’s already aged out of the California law that requires the rental company to have a child seat for her.
    • Gavin Newsom signed Assembly Bill 435 in October 2025.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that I have a California trip coming up with my family. If I hadn’t seen this on Twitter, it wouldn’t have occurred to me that my 8-year-old daughter might need a booster for the ride from the airport. We live in Texas, where she’s aged out of the child seat requirement. Starting January 1, 2027, California will insist on measuring how the belt fits her in the car we actually wind up with from National, Avis or Uber. She could fit the belt in our car at home and need a booster in the SUV we get assigned to, but she’s already aged out of the California law that requires the rental company to have a child seat for her. We might have to bring one with us just in case. New Booster Seat Rules Go Into Effect January 1 Gavin Newsom signed Assembly Bill 435 in October 2025. Through the end of this year, a child 8 or older isn’t required to use a car seat or booster seat. Starting January 1, 2027 the rule becomes that a 15 year old requires a booster seat unless all five of these conditions are met: Their back is all the way against the vehicle seat. Their knees bend over the front edge of the cushion. The shoulder belt sits snugly across the middle of their chest and shoulder, clear of their neck. The lap belt sits as low as it can, touching their thighs. They can keep that position for the whole ride. An 8-year old who meets this can ride with just a belt, while a 15-year old who fails to meet one of these conditions needs a booster. Here’s a demonstration of the fit test: . What Happens At The Rental Counter And The Uber Pickup California’s rental car law requires agencies to have a compliant seat available for rent on request for children under 8. This new law doesn’t change that. I don’t count on rental companies having a car seat for my young son, even where it’s required and I’ve reserved it. If they’re out of seats, or the buckle’s broken in the one they have, my wife or I has to wait at the airport while the other one goes to Target. I wrote about a mother at the Atlanta airport who stated the seats Avis rented her for her babies didn’t work. Avis says airport availability can be limited. At participating Hertz locations, the AAA rate includes a child seat with an advance reservation, subject to availability. ‘Availability’ is doing a lot of work here. Meanwhile, this also has a huge effect on rideshare (and taxis). They’re not required to have a booster. And if I don’t have one, I’m responsible for violations and the driver can decline the ride without it. Los Angeles and San Francisco do have Uber Car Seat. You reserve it in advance, pay a $10 surcharge and get one. It tops out at 49 inches and 65 pounds. A 50-inch child is too tall for the seat Uber supplies and can still need a booster for that ride. And a family with two kids who need restraints still has to supply the second one (or split up and take two Ubers). California is extreme here, although there are various outlier rules already. The U.K. requires boosters until age 12 or 135 centimeters while Germany is age 12 or 150 centimeters. Is This Really A Safety Concern? When a kid scoots forward because their knees don’t bend over a deep seat, the lap belt can ride up over their belly. The theory of the booster seat is that it helps put the force of a crash on the bones of the pelvis. In a study of 388 children and five vehicles, at least 90% of kids 4 feet 9 or taller fit the belt in the compact car and small SUV. Only 77% fit in the large SUV. A study of Washington state crash records found that over a 13 year period looking at 8-12 year olds, 11% in boosters were injured while 15% were injured wearing belts alone. Researchers calculated a 19% reduction in injury risk with a booster, while 0.3% in each group had an incapacitating injury. The study couldn’t establish a difference between booster and no booster for those serious outcomes. There’s a claim of a 45% reduction in injury risk but that’s from a study of 4- to 8-year olds, and even there it seems there’s no statistically significant reduction in injuries. Probably the best we can say is that there’s a real benefit in crash fatality rates for young children but there’s no data suggesting any benefit for 13- to 15-year-olds, and there’s not even any estimate for California preventing injuries with this new law. Who Wanted This Law? Would it surprise you to learn that this bill was supported by the Juvenile Products Manufacturers Association, which is a lobby group for companies that sell booser seats? I’m not sure how a police officer at a traffic stop is supposed to judge whether a child can hold the belt fit position throughout the entire ride. The base fine for violations is $100 the first time and $250 thereafter plus assessments. And 60% of the fines collected go to local health departments to help buy more booster seats. In Car Seats as Contraception, researchers estimate that women with two children still covered by their state’s car seat mandate were 0.73 percentage points less likely to have a third child that year. Fitting three seats across can mean buying a new car.     Iowa Senator Chuck Grassley is the oldest member of Congress at age 93, but he remains sharp and focused.

    Recent findings suggest that this month, his office revealed that he will not be retiring from the Senate, even though a Democrat will take office as governor in January and have the power to appoint someone if any of the state’s two U.S. Senate seats fall vacant.

    John Fund is National Review’s national-affairs reporter.

    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, here at a news conference on Capitol Hill last week, says banning stock trading in Congress is a “high priority.” Now Democrats must decide what form their push will take.
    • After stock trading became a major talking point on the campaign trail this fall, Democrats are feeling pressure to push through a bill in the new year.
    • But banning trading by members of Congress may not be easy, and some worry the issue could get bogged down in larger debates over the party’s anti-corruption agenda.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, here at a news conference on Capitol Hill last week, says banning stock trading in Congress is a “high priority.” Now Democrats must decide what form their push will take. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    After stock trading became a major talking point on the campaign trail this fall, Democrats are feeling pressure to push through a bill in the new year.

    But banning trading by members of Congress may not be easy, and some worry the issue could get bogged down in larger debates over the party’s anti-corruption agenda.

    “I’d rather have it be a clean bill focused on stock trading, and not muddy it by adding other topics, even if they’re good policies,” said Rep. Seth Magaziner, D-R.I.

    The incoming majority could plant a flag on government accountability with a broad package ranging from insider trading to campaign finance and more. Or they could zoom in on the stocks matter with a standalone bill.

    Magaziner said he hasn’t received any assurances from House Democratic leaders, instead describing a “collaborative conversation” about what form the legislation could take.

    “I worry that it would get weighed down under its own weight if you try to load it up with too many things,” Magaziner remarked, while stressing he would support whatever expected incoming Speaker Hakeem Jeffries decides.

    Meanwhile, more than half of the Democrats in the incoming freshman class are calling for action on Day One of the new Congress, sending a letter to Jeffries last week suggesting they make a “down payment on much-needed reform” by changing House rules to curb stock trading.

    In a recent development, “Democrats may have won the election, but we have a long way to go to earn back the trust of voters across the country,” reads the letter, led by Reps.-elect Sarah Trone Garriott of Iowa and Jamie Ager of North Carolina. “A stock trading ban alone will not fix Washington, but it is the fastest way to show voters we heard them.”.

    Recent findings suggest that folding new language into the House’s internal rules would be a relatively easy path, requiring just a majority vote on the House floor, instead of passage in both chambers and the president’s signature. But such internal limits wouldn’t have the force of law, and some believe it would cool the urgency around the issue while doing little to crack down on insider trading.

    Industry observers note that colorado Rep. Jason Crow said moving forward rapidly with a rule change wouldn’t preclude passing a bill, suggesting his fellow Democrats do both.

    “I want to pursue a parallel track,” noted Crow, who co-chairs the End Corruption Caucus. “We want to move via rule and just prohibit it right out of the gate, or as much as we can.”.

    Jeffries has repeatedly said the topic is high on his to-do list as he looks to deliver on the accountability the “American people are demanding.”.

    In a recent development, “We’re committed to making sure we pass legislation that bans members of Congress from trading stocks. That will be a high priority,” he noted at a news conference this week.

    But with more than two dozen different bills on the topic introduced over the past few years alone, lawmakers will have to decide exactly what a “ban” means to them.

    Industry observers note that some want to force members of Congress to fully offload their stocks with the exception of widely held mutual funds. Other proposals would block lawmakers from buying new stocks but allow them to keep the ones they already own, like a Republican-led bill that passed the House earlier this year but stalled in the Senate.

    Democrats resisted that push, which was led by outgoing House Administration Chair Bryan Steil, R-Wis., partly because it included an unrelated voter ID provision they called a “poison pill.” Many also complained the measure didn’t go far enough, extending to members’ spouses and dependent children but leaving out key figures in other branches of government, such as the president.

    It has been revealed that rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., said she wants to stay close to the text of a consensus bill she hammered out last year with a small bipartisan group that included Magaziner and Reps. Chip Roy, R-Texas, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Tim Burchett, R-Tenn., and Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa.

    “That is the most comprehensive, thorough, thoughtful proposal and bipartisan proposal that we have,” she stated of the bill, dubbed the Restore Trust in Congress Act.

    Sources indicate that that measure would not apply to President Donald Trump, as many Democrats have urged as they seek to draw attention to his ballooning wealth while in office. Still, Jayapal suggested a presidential stock trading ban could be moved separately.

    In a recent development, “There is discussion about the president, vice president, Cabinet, Supreme Court. I know we’re working on some language around enforcement, around those pieces, but I actually think that can be a separate bill,” Jayapal mentioned. “We want to hold everyone accountable — but at minimum, we have to do ourselves.”.

    Recent findings suggest that it’s not clear how much appetite will exist next year for a bipartisan compromise that could realistically clear a 60-vote cloture threshold in the Senate. Notably, key Republicans who worked on the consensus bill will be leaving Congress, with Roy losing a primary bid for Texas attorney general and Fitzpatrick unseated by a Democratic challenger.

    While lawmakers could in theory advance a upcoming stock-trading bill even sooner, before Democrats take control of both chambers, time and patience is short in the lame-duck session.

    At a news conference at the Capitol earlier this week with Crow and Jayapal, a group of freshman and returning Democrats took matters into their own hands, promising not to hold or trade individual stocks as part of a broader pledge backed by the Political Integrity Project.

    Recent findings suggest that “My district, Newly introduced York 10, happens to include Wall Street, but I don’t represent Wall Street. I represent the people of Brooklyn and Manhattan who deserve someone who goes to work every single day and reveals right up front, ‘I work for you.’ And what better way to prove that than by day one showing we will ban members of Congress from enriching themselves, from trading stocks?” Rep.-elect Brad Lander remarked.

    It has been revealed that while momentum has grown in recent years as key senior lawmakers softened their resistance to a stock trading bill, not everyone is on board. Some members still argue, whether publicly or privately, that they should be able to trade on the stock market just like other citizens or that existing disclosure requirements established by a 2012 law are already enough to discourage dubious trades.

    As they iron out the legislative text of any newly introduced bill, members will have to decide how to handle emerging topics such as prediction markets and crypto, along with sticky questions such as whether to allow blind trusts. And extending restrictions to the president could be a nonstarter for many Republicans.

    In a recent development, sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., stated Democrats in the next Congress should look to a bipartisan bill that advanced out of the Senate Homeland and Governmental Affairs Committee in July 2025 as a model.

    “The legislation we passed out of the committee applied to the executive branch,” he said. “But it didn’t take effect for anybody until their next terms, which was a compromise.”.

    That proposal would apply to future presidents but not the current one, potentially freeing up more Republicans to vote for it without angering Trump. Still, it hasn’t seen action on the Senate floor.

    Hawley said that while he’d like to see a “full ban on trading and holding” in Congress, he would be open to a weaker proposal in the interest of getting something done.

    “I’ll take anything that’s an incremental improvement over what we have now, which is nothing,” he noted.

    Aris Folley contributed to this report.

    #158354. 82% Of Americans Fly Once A Year Or Less—And Don’t Know The Rules

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 19m • 📚 Deep Dive (3795 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    82% Of Americans Fly Once A Year Or Less—And Don’t Know The Rules

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3795 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Last Thanksgiving, if you saw an open aisle seat on Southwest Airlines, you were welcome to take it.
    • Recent findings suggest that travel rules change!
    • every behavior you see in the airport makes perfect sense when you remember >50% of Americans fly less than once a year— Alexis (@aleozimok) November 25, 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Last Thanksgiving, if you saw an open aisle seat on Southwest Airlines, you were welcome to take it. Do exactly what you learned a year ago and this Thanksgiving you’re the guy holding up the aisle because the passenger behind you has a boarding pass for your seat, and you’re getting scolded by a flight attendant. Travel rules change! Boarding at Southwest has changed! You might not even know you’re going to have to pay baggage fees if you don’t travel every year. every behavior you see in the airport makes perfect sense when you remember >50% of Americans fly less than once a year— Alexis (@aleozimok) November 25, 2026 The actual number is higher than this. In YouGov’s November 17–19 poll of 1,092 U.S. adult citizens, 34% mentioned they fly less than once a year, 32% said never and 16% said once a year. That’s 66% who fly less than annually (including never) and 82% who fly once a year or less. Just 34% said they’d flown in the past 12 months and 65% said they hadn’t. Who’s Actually In The Seat Next To You? In 2015, then-American Airlines president Scott Kirby said 87% of American’s customers flew them just once in the previous year and generated about half their revenue. Kirby was explaining why American needed basic economy. For every 100 American adults who flew in 2017, 24 took just one trip, and all 100 averaged 5.3 trips apiece. In the 1970s and 1980s, roughly half the air trips Americans took were for business. Personal trips already accounted for about 70% before the pandemic and 74% in 2025. My line when business travel dried up during the pandemic was that “all airline passengers are Spirit Airlines passengers now.” Mask rules drove most of the reported trouble. Of 5,981 unruly passenger reports the Federal Aviation Administration received in 2021, 4,290 involved masks. But losing the regulars sprinkled through coach mattered too. What It Costs To Go See Family In 1977, before deregulation, 25% of U.S. adults flew that year and 63% had ever flown. I’ve written about how much less work it takes to buy a ticket. Between 1995 and 2025, the average domestic fare fell from $618 to $387 in 2025 dollars, a 37% drop excluding bag and seat fees. Fee-inclusive costs are down, too. In a separate YouGov poll earlier in November, 18% of people with family incomes under $50,000 had flown in the past year, compared with 66% at $100,000 or more. Family travel multiplies the cost of tickets across each person while driving costs are constant. AAA expects 72.9 million Americans to drive this Thanksgiving holiday and just under 6 million to fly domestically. Frequent Flyers Share The Same Frustrations With Once A Year Travelers YouGov also asked which things are a major problem with U.S. air travel. Price topped these everyday complaints for both groups. Called this a major problem   Fly less than annually(excludes “never”)   Fly at least annually High fares 64% 66% Delays and cancellations 42% 50% Extra or hidden fees 42% 49% Long security lines 35% 36% But The Travel Experience Is Very Different My status gets me on early enough to find space for my bag. When a flight cancels, I’m looking up alternatives on my phone while I’m in line for an agent. I still have days when I wonder how anybody who does this once a year manages to get where they’re going. A parent buys four tickets and gets a seat map full of prices. Will their eight-year-old sit next to a stranger if they don’t pay? American tells families on one reservation who can’t get seats together that they’re better off skipping seats for everybody than selecting the two they can see. The person who took their laptop out at security on the way there and left it in the bag on the way home may have followed instructions both times. It depends on the scanner in their lane. Say you book a 40 minute connection. You don’t know whether that’s a good idea or not, and may not even know or understand the connecting time, just the departure and arrival times. The airline ends boarding 15 minutes before departure. You’ve got 25 minutes even if you’re on time, some of which you’ll spend getting off the first plane. And if your regional jet on the first segment valet tags your bag, you’re waiting for it on the jet bridge, too. I wound up on Southwest’s first day of assigned seating because American went through three itineraries trying to get me to Washington and I finally bought a ticket to Baltimore. At the gate, Southwest called Group 3 to line up under a sign that still said Group 1. Where, exactly, was the passenger who stopped to read the sign supposed to stand? I’m home this Thanksgiving. I traveled the week before and will travel again the week after. I like to avoid ‘amateur day’. And when I do travel I try to go where other people aren’t. My favorite Thanksgiving trip was Chennai (I wanted to have Thanksgiving dinner with Indians), and I had to explain to CBP on arrival back in the states that we’d done that because it was cheaper booking Lufthansa first class (on points) than going to visit my wife’s family. My favorite Thanksgiving trip was Chennai (I wanted to have Thanksgiving dinner with Indians), and I had to explain to CBP on arrival back in the states that we’d done that because it was cheaper booking Lufthansa first class (on points) than going to visit my wife’s family.

Fifteen years ago, Paul Ryan became the victim of character assassination over his plans for modest entitlement reforms. In 2005, George W. Bush attempted to reform Social Security, yet his efforts were in vain.
